newsitem.title: CHINA: China to issue more overseas bonds.
newsitem.headline: China to issue more overseas bonds.

text.p: China's Ministry of Finance will make frequent issues of sovereign debt over the next few years, focusing on markets in the United States, Japan and Europe, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The issues would be part of a drive to build up China's position in the global capital market and provide a benchmark for other Chinese institutions to make overseas bond issues, the newspaper said.
It did not give any details of any offerings being planned in these key markets or say what it meant by frequent issues.
The ministry was also considering issues in Singapore, Australia and Hong Kong, the newspaper quoted Gao Jian, director of the ministry's debt management department, as saying.
"We will issue Hong Kong dollar bonds in Hong Kong at the proper time," Gao said without giving further details.
The offers would not significantly add to China's foreign debt, which stood at $106.59 billion as of the end of last year, Gao said.
China issued $1.0 billion of global bonds and $400 million of Yankee bonds this year and had raised $3.9 billion in sovereign debt since 1987, the newspaper said.
